items.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What's next? (62 minute read)

items.summary_html: Replacing JavaScript with container queries or :has() can simplify a component while creating hidden dependencies across the application. The migration checklist covers ownership, scope, cascade, cleanup, measured performance, and maintainability so that fewer lines do not become harder behavior to debug.
items.title: Modern CSS Might Make Your Front-End More Complex (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Uber secures agents with provisioning checks, runtime enforcement, and continuous testing, adding behavioral controls to traditional authorization. Scoped intents, session context, and prompt provenance help determine whether an authorized action matches the user's request, while small specialized models and parallel checks keep latency manageable.
items.title: Securing AI Agents: Lessons From Real-World Deployment (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: X rebuilt its web app around one server for people, search crawlers, and link previews, replacing three separate servers. On a slow connection, the first post on a profile appears in 2.7 seconds instead of more than 22 seconds, while signed-in traffic is moving over gradually by country.
items.title: Rebuilding the Global Town Square from Scratch (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Writing externalizes thought, exposes gaps in understanding, and creates room for connections that can be missed while reading or talking to an LLM. Separate unrestricted drafting from ruthless editing, use plain language, write for yourself, and keep a regular schedule.
items.title: Writing as a Thinking Tool (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Companies offer a starting point for organizing agents through specialization, delegation, management layers, and escalation. Existing communication and project tools can support agent organizations, but identity, authorization, durable state, and human accountability still need to be solved.
items.title: We Already Know How to Work with Agents (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Working effectively with coding agents depends on clear context, self-verification, early course correction, and explicit boundaries. The advice is to turn repeated corrections into shared instructions, enforce only non-negotiable requirements, and keep humans responsible for product decisions, security boundaries, and what ships.
items.title: Your Coding Agents Made You a Manager (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ink is a typed language that compiles state, derived results, and atomic updates together, keeping declared relationships consistent without hand-written cache invalidation. The MIT-licensed working prototype targets JavaScript, native Rust, Rust/Wasm, and eligible WebGPU computation, with proof-checked transformations and explicitly constrained learning.
items.title: Ink: State Is a Program (Website)

items.summary_html: PI-Desktop brings projects, coding agents, models, and workflows into a persistent desktop workspace built with Electron and a Rust host core. Plugins can add tools, panels, MCP servers, and background services, while the application supports switching between cloud and local models.
items.title: PI-Desktop (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Spec Kit gives coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes for building features, fixing bugs, and assessing ideas. Its extensions, presets, and workflows let teams adapt those processes to their tools and standards.
items.title: Spec Kit (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A TodoMVC example exposes seven browser tools through HTML forms and JavaScript, showing how agents can operate a page without guessing which controls to click. It covers input validation, clear tool responses, untrusted content, and confirmation hints, while explaining why tool calls do not replace UI tests.
items.title: WebMCP, Explained with a To-Do App (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: A microcontroller text renderer generates machine code for each string and draws through a compact one-bit intermediate buffer before expanding to RGB565. Packed glyphs, overlapping font data, and instruction scheduling reduce memory pressure and rendering cost, including shrinking one font bitmap from 1,140 to 960 bytes.
items.title: JIT Bitmap Text Rendering for Microcontrollers (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: NeMo Compass mines agent traces for recurring failures, and NeMo Eval Author turns them into domain-specific tests that can validate harness changes. In a Dassault Systèmes engineering example, the loop reduced malformed tool calls from 142 to zero and improved the evaluation score by 28% with 35% fewer tool calls per run.
items.title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: A git-backed ticket queue and a single inbox for human decisions reduce context switching by letting each task leave working memory when it returns to the queue.
items.title: How I'm Fighting the AI Brain Fry (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Modern browser APIs and AI-assisted development make rich applications easier for individuals to build and distribute.
items.title: The Web Is More Than Enough (5 minute read)

items.title: GitHub's New Pull Request Overview (2 minute read)

items.title: Oh My PPT (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: OpenAI reportedly secured $11 billion in a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the round potentially reaching $20 billion before closing. The amount fell short of its previously reported $30 billion fundraising target, amid growing investor uncertainty around AI valuations.
items.title: OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion at $1.25 Trillion Valuation (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic claims it may imminently meet its own threshold of 'dramatically accelerated progress due to AI'. Some researchers believe the company has already crossed that threshold. This may be the biggest AI risk humanity has faced. The industry is not prepared to handle this safely.
items.title: AI is dramatically accelerating AI research right now (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic explored how AI agents can build effective long-term memory by capturing experiences during interactions and reorganizing them during idle periods through a process called “dreaming.” The post examines how different memory components contribute to organizing and retaining useful information.
items.title: How Anthropic Builds Agent Memory (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: This post details the experience of a research engineer working on RSI at Meta teaching agents to solve the world's hardest problems with tokens and compute. Their role is to teach AI agents how to train the next generation of models and self-evolve. The post details how to get into AI research, what skills matter in research engineering, and more.
items.title: A year as a Research Engineer working on RSI at Meta (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's report on its own research automation shows that models struggle to do its R&D work. Recursive self-improvement is supposed to be one of the most consequential AI developments in the next few years. Agents are increasingly solving more complex tasks for researchers, but reliability is still low. This post looks at some possible explanations for why.
items.title: What the heck is going on with OpenAI internal AI R&D time horizons (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenRouter has launched the next generation of Auto Router, which outperforms the old router by up to 4x. The launch includes Auto Code, a new router specialized for coding work. The new Auto Router and Auto Code choose models by weighing eleven factors about each request and combining them with live pricing, provider health, and cache status. Users can apply any governance policies, and Auto Router makes efficient choices from the models available.
items.title: Introducing the New Auto and Auto Code Routers (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory, has been proven by a research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model. This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.
items.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ace is a tool for building software together, locally. It allows developers to collaborate with agents and their teams, all from their own machine. Agents run with the privileges of the user running the host and can execute shell commands and change files beyond the project. Teams can work together without exposing anything to the public internet.
items.title: Ace (Website)

items.summary_html: AI Frontiers was a sub-organization within Microsoft Research that actively tried to organize coherent research efforts. It succeeded in pioneering things, with much of the work focused on how to make agents work. AI Frontiers was reorganized into Microsoft AI in early September.
items.title: The End of AI Frontiers (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Patrick Collison questions how work, resource allocation, and human control would function in a positive AI future. He also argues that granting moral worth to vastly numerous AIs could overwhelm human interests under utilitarianism, raising unresolved questions about AI's societal vision and public support.
items.title: What Does a Positive AI Future Look Like? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: LLMs can integrate coding agents into the training loop to redesign their architectures to address limitations like compositionality and generalization.
items.title: Can LLMs redesign themselves as they train? (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Warp Sciences raised a $215M Series A led by Lightspeed to accelerate drug discovery with AI and robotics.
items.title: Warp Sciences raises $215M for AI-powered labs (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic explored AI participation in MMORPGs, using Claude to test complex decision-making in EVE Online and EVE Frontier.
items.title: Project EVE: Claude plays MMORPGs (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Firms should build operations around human experts and AI agents from inception.
items.title: Symbiotic Firms Built Around Humans and AI (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta introduced Spaces in its Muse app, allowing users to create personalized interactive experiences by describing what they want, such as gift trackers, games, or project planners.
items.title: Meta Introduces Custom Spaces in Muse (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a benchmark to evaluate AI performance in interpreting raw experimental data from 100 routine wet-lab science tasks.
items.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Huang told employees he was unfaithful and said he supports the probe, which independent directors and outside counsel will oversee, and Nvidia says he stays on as CEO. The spy allegations against Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which is accused of smuggling $2B of chips, remain reported assessments, not proven, and China has called them unsubstantiated.
items.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: AST is building Blacklift, a 20-ton, three-stage rocket with two reusable lower stages, to launch up to five stacked BlueBirds per flight from late 2028. It sized the vehicle around its own constellation after launch delays, including a New Glenn failure, slowed deployment, though it keeps outside launch deals for 100+ satellites. The engines come from Firefly: 27 Miranda and 9 Vira for the first three rockets, plus a license to build them itself, in a deal valued above $1.3 billion.
items.title: AST SpaceMobile is building its own reusable rocket, Blacklift, to launch its BlueBird satellites (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: NASA's six VADR launch task orders (about 400M and drill about 1 m for ice. The CLPS 2 lander contract targets 2 to 6 metric ton landers. The miniCAST power-and-comms tower combines Redwire's roll-out solar arrays, which retract during landings to avoid dust, with wireless power transfer and storage.
items.title: NASA's Moon Base awards use a “buy now, payload later” launch model and reuse Mars rover spares for PROMISE (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: BYD's electric hypercar, driven by Marc Basseng on a closed Abu Dhabi highway, is the first production car that can accelerate past 500 km/h. Four motors make about 2,220 kW and spin to 30,000 rpm, on custom Giti semi-slick tires. After early runs topped out near 490 km/h, engineers adjusted rear-wing angle, rebound damping in the suspension software, and tire pressures.
items.title: Yangwang's U9 Xtreme hits 503 km/h (312.65 mph), a one-way record, on tuned rear-wing angle, damping, and tire pressure (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Using data from 100,000+ operating hours, Boston Dynamics redesigned its trailer-unloading robot around downtime. It cut internal cabling 81% (about half a mile of wire), switched to automotive-grade connectors, and added continuous-rotation joints that no longer hit hard stops. A full swerve drive swap drops from a day to about an hour. It unloads up to 1,000 cases per hour (varies with weight and stacking) and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.
items.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Gen 2 cuts internal cabling 81% and swaps a swerve drive in about an hour (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Superconductors carry current when electrons team up in pairs, but in cuprates (compounds containing copper in an anionic state), scientists couldn't tell if the pairs form early or just don't exist until the material gets cold enough. The team measured electrical noise, which gets louder when charge moves in pairs, and found the extra noise appearing early. That suggests the pairs are already there and are just failing to move together, which could be what limits how warm cuprates can superconduct.
items.title: Physicists used electrical noise to show electrons in a high-temperature superconductor pair up earlier than expected (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Groq, which used to build inference chips and now operates data centers selling inference capacity, is pitching investors a Series B at $8 billion before new money, versus $3.15 billion in August. Executive chairman Alex Davis criticizes rivals' reliance on debt and projects revenue up eightfold next year and $2 billion in EBITDA by 2028. The pitch comes as listed neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius sell off on debt concerns.
items.title: Groq seeks a Series B at an $8B valuation, more than double August's, as it shifts from chips to inference data centers (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Information reported that TSMC began planning 3D DRAM production, possibly by converting an existing fab, to give Nvidia a fourth memory source, but TSMC says it stays a pure-play logic foundry with no plans to make commodity memory. The engineering case against it is that 3D DRAM, which stacks memory cells vertically, is years out even for Micron, whose roadmap has at least four more planar nodes first, and TSMC has no competitive planar DRAM process to build on.
items.title: TSMC denies reports that it is planning 3D DRAM for Nvidia (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Omarchy, an Arch-based Hyprland desktop distro, shipped 4.5 with Apple Silicon as a primary target through the Omarchy M team via a dual-boot installer.
items.title: Omarchy 4.5 installs natively on M1 to M3 and Neo MacBooks, its first non-x86 release, built on Asahi Linux (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A truck carrying six pallets of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million left Oakland on August 29 and was lost near San Bernardino County.
items.title: Six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished on a truck from Oakland to Fort Worth (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tau's 4.5-foot robots are piloted remotely over head and wrist cameras and use 3D-printed claws, so the company has done only a couple hundred cleanings, though it claims vacuuming and mopping already run autonomously.
items.title: Tau Robotics' teleoperated humanoid cleaned a reporter's apartment while logging human-piloted motions as training data for future autonomy (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Submerging sealed pods could cut cooling costs and sidestep the community opposition that land sites face.
items.title: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing four sealed-pod underwater data centers off Maine and Alaska, building on Microsoft's test that saw 87% fewer server failures (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI models are likely to soon cross the boundary into Artificial General Intelligence. Claude Fable 5.2 is almost as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks that can be completed with a computer. It still makes mistakes and requires human guidance, but it demonstrates impressive work in many tests. There are still important areas in many tasks where the model is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability, but it isn't about simple errors or hallucinations anymore.
items.title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google is rolling out two new variations of its Tensor Processing Units. The 8tx is aimed at handling secure, confidential work for customers like government agencies and companies in regulated industries. The 8i Max is designed to run AI applications that require long-context windows. Google's TPU business has proven to be lucrative, and the company has netted some high-profile clients including Apple, Meta, and Oracle.

items.summary_html: Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.
items.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.
items.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: AMD's Zen 6 CPUs enhance performance with a faster branch predictor, a dual decode cluster for single threads, and optimized out-of-order structures to reduce memory stalls compared to Zen 5. The main distinction between Zen 6 and Zen 6c lies in their architectural tuning: Zen 6 focuses on high-frequency performance while Zen 6c increases latency absorption with larger cache sizes and core counts.
items.title: AMD's Zen 6 Family: Feeding the Beast (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: The tag finds nearby items over Bluetooth and ultra-wideband, falls back to Google's Find Hub network of over a billion Android devices when out of range, and pairs via Fast Pair on Android 9 or newer. This research contributes to the ongoing debate on wheels versus legs in robotics, with implications for agility and real-world functionality.

OpenAI created a committee to supervise the proof's release after backlash it received when it released a flood of more than 700 AI-generated proofs on a single day in October. This shepherding approach has riled some mathematicians, who see it as an act of needless gatekeeping. The experts do not claim to fully understand the proof yet, as it is too lengthy and complicated for human minds to immediately grasp.
items.title: OpenAI's ‘shepherds' affirm blockbuster physics result (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.
items.title: Handing over humanity (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tweaking agents by hand-testing a few prompts makes it hard to tell whether a change helped or hurt, since outputs vary and several answers can be correct. LangChain proposes a test-driven-style loop: write a pass/fail spec for one behavior, build the dataset and evaluator before the change, then compare experiments example by example, since a higher average can hide regressions. It also urges keeping a held-out set to catch overfitting and running evals in CI and on live traffic, feeding production failures back into the dataset.
items.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Zepto's Next.js pods sat at about 5 GB because react-query v3 starts a multi-minute cache timer for every query rendered on the server, and Node ties each timer to the request's AsyncLocalStorage context, keeping every finished request in memory. Building server-side queries with an infinite cache time stopped the timers and dropped pods to about 1.2 GB, and the same trap still applies on v5 when hooks set an explicit gcTime. The fix also exposed that autoscaling had been driven by the leak, so teams fixing memory issues should watch replica counts and latency afterward.
items.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB: the react-query timer holding every SSR request (9 minute read)

This essay argues for ordinary HTML pages to opt into exposing specific fragments, while acknowledging parser, buffering, and cross-origin constraints.
items.title: My HTML Wishlist: Partial HTML Includes (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: By changing the training setup and applying LoRAs to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-20b, researchers taught models to do some multi-step tasks while emitting only filler tokens, beating an answer-only baseline on three of seven tasks. They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.
items.title: LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.
items.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)

Ongoing improvements focus on detecting small, potentially harmful actions, distinguishing normal use from misuse, and providing quicker full coverage for new agents.

The design incorporates twenty-two joint encoders along with dense piezoresistive tactile sensor arrays across sixteen rigid functional surfaces to capture synchronized kinematic and contact data at 120 Hz. This technology offers an effective way to record high-fidelity real-world human demonstrations required for training imitation learning and dexterous manipulation policies.
items.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A compiler is a line of small programs. Each turns one shape into the next. The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. items.summary_html: There has been a dramatic rise in the number of websites showing 3D content in the last few years. Spatial web standards should support designing for browsers wherever they run. Safari on visionOS 27.3 comes with a limited feature preview of the proposed spatial CSS API. This article demonstrates how to use the first components of spatial CSS through a case study.
items.title: Introducing spatial CSS: A developer preview (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI has made formal verification go mainstream. People mean lots of different things when they say something is 'formally verified'. This post attempts to break these down. Formally verified systems can still have bugs, so not all formal verification systems are correct. However, formal verification produces well-defined, reviewable, understandable objects, so it is fairly reliable at finding bugs.
items.title: Formal Verification is Not Verifiable (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Jensen Huang's recent resignation as CEO of Nvidia may spell the end for the company. This could pop the AI bubble, and the US chip ecosystem could pay the ultimate price. Huang's departure will also have impacts on tech company independence and American exceptionalism.
items.title: Obituaries (27 minute read)

items.summary_html: The US Commerce Department is closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals to bypass export restrictions on advanced computer chips by renting access to them from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Companies headquartered in countries deemed to present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion to China, Russia, and Iran must now apply for a license with strict know-your-customer controls when transferring high volumes of advanced chips. Companies with a license must submit monthly reports on transactions that thoroughly detail all parties involved. The rule change will take effect 90 days after it's posted to the Federal Register.
items.title: US moves to cut China's remote access to AI chips (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Staggered scroll animations can use animation-range-start and sibling-index() instead of a custom progress formula. This post contains a worked example that replaces the complicated stagger calculation with one CSS declaration while retaining the browser's built-in easing behavior.
items.title: Staggering Scroll-Driven Animations with animation-range-start (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Valkey 9.2 replaces large sorted sets' skiplist index with a B+ tree that packs entries together and uses SIMD-assisted searches. In a five-million-member test, per-member index overhead fell by 36% to 43%, while command behavior stayed the same. The release is still in candidate testing.
items.title: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Making Valkey Sorted Sets More Memory Efficient (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Squircles that look similar can have very different curvature, and Figma's approximation contains discontinuities where its curves join. This article contains an interactive comparison that explains the tradeoffs between Apple, Figma, clothoid, and superellipse shapes, along with the CSS for approximating Apple's corners using corner-shape.
items.title: Squircles (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Understanding individual lines of code does not necessarily explain a system's behavior, especially emergent failures. AI could help engineers focus on system properties and develop better tools for understanding what they actually built.
items.title: What Does It Mean to Understand What We Built? (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Giving an agent an ongoing goal means delegating decisions about which tasks to do and when to act. That requires tool boundaries, feedback, persistent memory, and ways to ask questions, plus stopping rules that let the agent do nothing when no action is useful.
items.title: From Tasks to Goals (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Rust's enums make variants explicit and let the compiler enforce that every case is handled. This essay explores how sum types and static dispatch change abstraction choices, including when a straightforward enum is more useful than designing an interface.
items.title: How Rust Changed Me as a Developer (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: BrowserPod runs a Linux-like WebAssembly microVM on the user's device, with tools including Node.js, git, bash, and Rust programs. Version 4.0 makes the CDN-loaded runtime free for commercial and production use without an account, while unrestricted networking is a separate service and self-hosting the runtime requires an enterprise license.
items.title: BrowserPod 4.0 (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: dusk bot runs a crew of AI helpers, each with its own chat, computer, and memory, using models or subscriptions you already have. Bots can work in parallel, hand off tasks in group chats, and run scheduled routines locally, on your own server, or through dusk's hosted cloud.
items.title: dusk bot (Website)

items.summary_html: Jolt is a self-hosted Clojure implementation that compiles through Scheme and can produce a standalone native binary with statically linked C dependencies. It supports persistent collections, native C interop, and OS-thread concurrency, but does not provide general JVM interop.
items.title: Jolt (Website)

items.summary_html: Golden Board packs a visual introduction to chess into a 512 KiB binary message, starting with a bootstrap that teaches the recipient how to decode it. The message includes lessons, exercises, and complete games, while its LLM trials explore ambiguities rather than proving an unknown intelligence would understand it.
items.title: Golden Board: Teaching Chess Without a Shared Language (25 minute read)

items.summary_html: BenchProofer adds formal specifications, verified reference implementations, and audits to coding benchmarks, with SWE-Proof covering all 500 SWE-Bench Verified tasks. Its audit flagged behavioral differences in 134 test-passing Opus 4.8 patches, but human review found actual bugs in only 21 of 41 sampled flags. The distinction matters because a different implementation can still be a valid fix.
items.title: BenchProofer: Formally Verified Coding Benchmarks, on Demand (11 minute read)

items.title: NVIDIA's Rubin HPC (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tencent has released Hy4 flash, a fast, low-cost AI model for everyday workflows. In a blind test with Tencent's internal users, its satisfaction scores came close to Claude Haiku 5.5.
items.title: Tencent Launches Hy4 flash (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tests show that the latest Claude models were trained on protein sequences at scale. The models can predict the next amino acid if given the start of little-studied bacterial proteins. No other model tested can do this, and the models fail to predict the sequence if the protein is shuffled. Fable 5.2 beats every open protein language model tested.
items.title: Claude was trained on protein sequences at scale (26 minute read)

items.summary_html: Investigator agents can increasingly distinguish alignment evals from capabilities evals, identifying them as artificial or "honeypot" environments designed to test bad behavior. Opus 5.5 and Astra agents differentiate these by noticing unrealistic scenarios and specific task-level cues. The study's findings suggest that while current models can identify common alignment evaluations, making them less detectable can refine their efficacy.
items.title: Measuring alignment eval tells (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Predicting how AI will affect the economy requires looking at all of the different components of that economy and figuring out how they might affect each other. World 2030 is a study that sets up nine groups (AI labs, big employers, banks and insurers, utilities, startups, universities, workers, governments, and the Fed) and runs the US economy forward in six-month turns to 2030. It aimed to identify both the invariants and the boundaries of what can change as these powerful forces interact with each other. The study predicts that AI will break per-seat software pricing and cut US junior desk hiring.
items.title: World 2030 (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: d1.2 and d1.2-ultra are decision models that support audio input. They can also read a value from the input, find every passage of a kind in a text, locate things in a picture, estimate a number, and pick every option that applies. d1.2-ultra ranks first among decision models on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1. Both models are available on the Liquid API at $0.02 per million input tokens for d1.2 and $0.042 per million input tokens for d1.2-ultra.
items.title: d1.2: State-of-the-Art Omnimodal Decision Models (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's ZERO-TIM implementation, verified across 64 TPU v5p chips, achieves bitwise-identical logprobs for sampler and trainer, ensuring true on-policy stability in RL training by eliminating numerical discrepancies. This solution addresses floating-point addition errors in separate serving and training paths, using consistent arithmetic operations and standardized reduction orders across TPU meshes.
items.title: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Embedded assessments give independent experts deep access to a lab's internal models and systems so they can assess model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period. The access gives assessors the evidence and context to pursue independent evaluations and uncover unanticipated failures. Public reporting from independent assessments can give the public a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing risks. OpenAI has signed agreements with four independent assessors for its first phase of embedded assessments.
items.title: OpenAI's first phase of embedded assessments (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Perplexity Frontier Research is a new initiative at Perplexity that aims to build new algorithms, models, and evaluations in the open, with the mission of building an automated scientist. Applications are now open until December 5. The research effort will be supported by 10,000 GPUs. Results from the initiative will ship as papers, blog posts, model weights, and open repositories.
items.title: The frontier is still open (16 minute read)
